title: Scrubbing a long edit never trails the pointer by more than one display frame
goal: Dragging the playhead over the 6 minute reference edit keeps up most of the time (the picture is one refresh behind the hand at the middle), but at its worst it is still 3 to 5 refreshes behind. Make even the worst moment of a drag show the moment under the pointer within one display frame, at a medium end to end drag and while hunting back and forth.
notes: Carried from a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed (closed 2026-11-23). lag = refreshes since the hand was at the moment the picture carries (a stand-in frame counts as caught up); frame lag = the exact frame under the hand; sight lag = the frames the picture is really drawn from (SpeedWalk.ScrubTally). The medium drag's frame lag and sight lag worst are shown but not judged since 2026-11-23 (SpeedCompare.isJudged: 17 to 81 at the median on unchanged code); its lag worst is judged. Passes 20 to 22 made the hunt follow the hand (MovieSweep.window(follows:), restingPass, MovieFrameQueue.placesStillShown): hunt frame worst 43 -> 3. Lead from pass 22: the hunt's ~20 ms looks with an idle main thread (display link or render server; Metal System Trace needs developer mode). Lag worst 3-10 on medium in 45 runs: which moment is late is chance, so look at the per-look dump (temporary) before changing anything.
acceptance: Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh on the 6 minute edit reads scrub lag worst of 1 for the medium drag and the hunt, worst of three runs (2026-11-23: medium 5, hunt 3; medians already 1)
The hunt's frame lag and sight lag worst read 1 or 2 (2026-11-23: 3 and 3)

Reproduced 2026-11-25 on b2706336c, short speed walk: medium lag 1/5, hunt lag 1/3, hunt frame/sight worst 3/3, longest refresh 34 and 26 ms. A per-look dump (temporary) plus the pass sampler handed every gap between looks over 14 ms showed three causes: (1) the canvas picture and the four playhead islands (line, scrub bar, time, scroller mark) each made a top-level Core Animation commit, about 5 a refresh in a medium drag, and the window server let one wait 8 to 30 ms (mach send in CA::Context::commit_transaction) about once a drag, early in it; (2) the walk's own 50-a-second window-list look (sendWindowsBehindThePerson) blocks for the last frame to land, 108 of 290 ms across 24 slow gaps, a cost a person's app never has; (3) isolated looks where the composite of the move just made takes 6 to 8 ms and lands about 1 ms after the next look (154 of 177 remaining lag-2 looks).

Fixes: CATransaction.inThisTurnsCommit (Sources/Photonz/OneCommitPerTurn.swift) opens the turn's implicit transaction and nests the island repaint and CanvasNSView.showPlayingPicture inside it, so a refresh's layer changes go in one commit; PlaytestHarness.holdWindowWatch/letWindowWatchGo hold the window-list look while a scrub is on the clock (it already stays out of the main thread meter for the same reason), looking once when let go. Scrub-only walk, 4 drags each: commit change alone medium 3,3,2,3 hunt 4,3,3,2; with the hold medium 2,2,2 hunt 2,3,2. Tried and reverted: a cacheIntermediates:false CIContext for surface frames (draw p95 7-8 ms either way).

Pass 3 (ccc85f045). Per-look dump (temporary, removed) showed most mid-drag late looks were composites at transitions taking 7-9 ms against a 7.6 ms window. Pass 4 cause found. Medium drags stalled 12-22 ms at look 4-6 in 6 of 6 drags (12-drag scrub-only walk). Experiments, each over 6 medium + 6 hunt drags on a rebuilt probe: a 0.3 s wait after beginPlayheadDrag removed it (0/6), so not GPU warmth (an earlier GPU-warm result was a stale probe: playtest.sh --no-build reuses the bundle); skipping beginScrubAudition removed it (0/6, early late looks 22 -> 1); skipping only ScrubAudioEngine's engine.start() removed it (0/6); keeping the engine running between drags left only the first drag's (1/6). Triage question answered: not the same hold as no-frame-of-a-50-track-zoom-is-held-up-by-the-sy. Here the main thread itself blocked in mach_msg send inside commit_transaction (stepTransactionFlush), set off by AVAudioEngine.start() about 40 ms earlier; the zoom's is the main thread on RenderBox's queue while a worker waits in RB::SharedSurfaceGroup::prune_removed_locked -> waitForCommitId. Removing the audio start removed this one entirely, so the two do not share a cause.
